title: 6850 ACIA
body:
**Keyboard Controller Chip**
[[IKBD Systems]]

An **Asynchronous Communications Interface Adapter**: a [[UART]] on a chip, converting
between the [[Motorola 68000]]'s parallel [[Bus]] and a serial line. The Atari ST has two,
one for the keyboard and one for MIDI.

Four registers as far as the programmer is concerned, two readable and two writable at the
same pair of addresses: a [[Status Register|status register]] (is a byte waiting, is the
transmitter free, was there a framing or parity error, was there an [[overrun]]) and a data
register (the byte itself). You either spin on the status register, which is [[Polling]], or
let it raise an interrupt through the [[68901 MFP]].

The byte it hands you for a keypress is a scan code, not [[ASCII]]; translating it is
software's job.

[[I-O Interface]] · [[Baud Rate]] · [[COMPUTING MACHINERY 2]] · [[COMPUTING MACHINERY]]
